# Ospf Router (Resource)

Manages an OSPF router in the UniFi controller. An OSPF router announces the networks assigned to its areas to neighbouring routers and can redistribute BGP, connected and static routes.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `areas` (Attributes List) OSPF areas this router participates in. The controller refuses a router with no areas. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--areas))
- `router_id` (String) The router's OSPF identifier, in dotted-quad form. The controller refuses an empty one.

### Optional

- `announce_default_route` (Boolean) Whether the router announces a default route to its neighbours.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the OSPF router is enabled.
- `interfaces` (Attributes List) Per-interface OSPF settings, keyed by the network the interface serves. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interfaces))
- `redistribute_bgp_routes` (Boolean) Whether routes learned over BGP are redistributed into OSPF.
- `redistribute_connected_routes` (Boolean) Whether directly connected routes are redistributed into OSPF.
- `redistribute_connected_routes_metric_type` (String) The OSPF metric type used when redistributing connected routes.
- `redistribute_static_routes` (Boolean) Whether static routes are redistributed into OSPF.
- `redistribute_static_routes_metric_type` (String) The OSPF metric type used when redistributing static routes.
- `site` (String) The name of the site to associate the OSPF router with.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the OSPF router.

<a id="nestedatt--areas"></a>
### Nested Schema for `areas`

Required:

- `network_ids` (List of String) IDs of the networks announced into this area.

Optional:

- `area_id` (String) The OSPF area identifier, in dotted-quad form (`0.0.0.0` is the backbone area).
- `area_type` (String) The area's type.
- `name` (String) A human-readable name for the area.


<a id="nestedatt--interfaces"></a>
### Nested Schema for `interfaces`

Optional:

- `authentication_type` (String) The interface's OSPF authentication type.
- `cost` (String) The interface's OSPF cost.
- `dead_interval` (String) Seconds without a hello before a neighbour on this interface is declared down.
- `hello_interval` (String) Seconds between hello packets on this interface.
- `network_id` (String) The ID of the network whose interface these settings apply to.
- `passive_interface` (Boolean) Whether the interface is passive: its networks are announced but no OSPF packets are sent on it.
- `priority` (String) The router's priority in designated-router election on this interface.


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
